options: Only the color palette of dashboards
Ownership, change control, and access rules for metric definitions
Only the speed of queries
Only who may log in to Salesforce
questions.explain: Governance is about who owns a definition, how changes are approved and communicated, and who is allowed to edit it.

questions.q: Who should typically be the owner of a metric such as Closed Won Revenue?
options: Whoever happened to build it
Any consumer of the metric
A named accountable business team, such as Revenue Operations
The person with the newest laptop
questions.explain: The owner is the person or team accountable for the definition, usually a business function rather than the builder.

questions.q: In Tableau Next, how do you keep several teams on one official definition without copying it?
options: Email a screenshot of the formula to each team
Reference the shared semantic model from other workspaces instead of duplicating it
Paste the calculation into every dashboard
Ask each team to rebuild it from memory
questions.explain: An asset lives in one workspace and can be referenced from others, so a central model stays the single source of truth.

questions.q: Why announce a metric definition change to consumers, per the change process?
options: So people understand what changed and from what date, and can interpret period-over-period comparisons
Because Salesforce requires an email for every edit
To hide the change from executives
Because the metric is automatically deleted otherwise
questions.explain: Without an announcement, numbers before and after the change silently stop matching and trust erodes.

questions.q: A user has Viewer access to a shared workspace. What does the lesson say about the underlying data objects?
options: Viewer access automatically grants access to every data object
Data objects are deleted when a workspace is shared
Only Owners can ever see data
Access to data objects is controlled separately in Data 360, so data governance and metric governance are two layers
questions.explain: Workspace sharing controls analytics assets; data object access is governed by policies in Data 360.
